source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Unfortunately, the earlier proposal is beyond my budget and includes more scope than I need. Could the simpler version instead focus on a single formatting/layout pass over the final draft, using Civic Canopy's existing brand colors and fonts, followed by one round of revisions and delivery as a print-ready PDF?

More specifically, what I need is 1) layout and graphic treatment for the complete document and 2) application of the tables, photos, org chart, and graphics to the final draft.

Because the RFQ is usually the first step, I suspect there is also a chance that an RFP will follow later. What would this reduced version cost?

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Leona,

Two points need your guidance as you review the attached first draft of the proposal:

\- **Section 11: Prioritization:** Because this section did not appear in the updated tables document, I’m still unsure whether it belongs in the proposal.

\- **In-text bolding:** The intended bold formatting was also unclear. Some passages in the Google Doc were highlighted while others appeared in red, and after moving into layout, I couldn’t determine which treatments were intentional and which were editorial markup.

The editable Canva version is available here: <https://design.blue-mesa.example/civic-canopy-brief-4821>

For context on the visual approach, the document grew roughly threefold while the timeline remained tight, so I built a consistent design system instead of creating numerous unique layouts. That consistency should also make revisions easier to manage. To support the overall theme without distracting from the content, I used organic-shaped image frames along with a few understated graphic elements.

Separately, all hyperlinks were tested and appeared to work, though I’d appreciate having a second reviewer click through each one as well.

Given the tight turnaround, I’ll make another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to catch anything I missed, but I wanted to get this to you today.

I look forward to your feedback. Hopefully the proposal is in a good place, and once you’ve reviewed it, I can fine-tune anything you want adjusted.

ambiguity.description: The source formatting does not establish which highlighted or red passages require intentional bolding and which are editorial markup.
